headline: Dry and very warm through Friday, with highs in the upper 70s to mid 80s (10–15 degrees above normal) and gusty north-to-northeast winds peaking on Thanksgiving in the LA valleys and mountains, while a big swell and very high tides bring a significant coastal flooding threat Wednesday and Thursday; light rain is possible Sunday night into Monday and a stronger, wetter storm is likely next Tuesday into Wednesday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Wednesday stays dry and sunny around Glendale and the LA basin, with light offshore (land-to-sea) winds this morning that strengthen through the day and overnight in the usual Santa Ana wind spots of LA and Ventura Counties. It turns very warm, part of a stretch through Friday with highs in the upper 70s to mid 80s, about 10–15 degrees above normal. Forecasters are watching how the winds develop today and tonight before deciding whether to widen Thursday's Wind Advisory.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Offshore winds peak on Thanksgiving (Thursday), but with an unusually strong push from the north as well as the east, which typically means less wind on the Oxnard/Ventura plain and stronger winds through the Grapevine, the western San Fernando Valley, Simi Valley and the Santa Monica Mountains. A Wind Advisory is in effect from 6 AM to 2 PM Thursday for the Santa Susana and western San Gabriel Mountains, and it may be expanded to more areas such as the Santa Monica Mountains and the Santa Clarita, San Fernando and Simi Valleys. Friday morning will still be gusty, though advisories are much less likely, and with warm air aloft and downhill-warmed winds, Thanksgiving and Friday are the hottest days, with Friday reaching the mid 80s across the LA valleys.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: The high pressure that brought the warmth breaks down and shifts east this weekend, cooling temperatures to near normal by Sunday. The tail end of a storm aimed mainly at Northern California will likely bring some light rain Sunday night into Monday, mostly under half an inch. A stronger storm is likely next Tuesday into Wednesday, tapping subtropical moisture as a weak atmospheric river (a long plume of moisture streaming in from the Pacific), with about a 1-in-4 chance of a moderate-strength one; current guidance shows widespread totals of at least 1–2 inches, up to 5 inches in 6–8 hours on mountain slopes facing the incoming winds, likely some thunderstorms, and snow only above about 8,000 feet. With record-warm ocean temperatures and the heavy downpours from earlier storms this season, forecasters have reasonable concern about flooding.

coast: The biggest concern this week is at the beaches. A large, long-period west swell peaks Wednesday and Thursday and combines with very high tides to bring large surf and moderate to significant coastal flooding, worst around high tide and in low-lying spots with no protection from the ocean. The highest surf and worst flooding are expected on the Central Coast from Point Conception northward, the Ventura County coast and far eastern parts of the southern Santa Barbara County coast, where Coastal Flood and High Surf Warnings run until noon Thursday; other beaches, including LA County, see somewhat lesser but still concerning impacts under Coastal Flood and High Surf Advisories through Thursday, plus a Coastal Flood Watch Thursday morning for some zones. Expect many strong rip currents nearly everywhere, strong along-shore currents, sneaker waves, heavy shore break, coastal erosion and an increased risk of damage to coastal structures, making swimming dangerous. Offshore, Small Craft Advisories run through 3 PM Thursday: outer-water seas peak at 14–19 feet today and inner waters north of Point Sal at 13–17 feet, with strong winds in the western Santa Barbara Channel Wednesday and from Point Mugu to Santa Monica Thursday; large breaking waves near harbor entrances can capsize small boats. Winds ease below advisory levels for most areas Friday through Sunday, though rough seas may linger in the outer waters (50–70% chance).
watch_for: Significant coastal flooding and dangerous surf at high tide Wednesday and Thursday, worst on the Central Coast and Ventura County coast.
Gusty north winds Thanksgiving in the LA valleys and mountains; the Wind Advisory may be expanded to the Santa Monica Mountains and Santa Clarita, San Fernando and Simi Valleys.
The likely Tuesday–Wednesday storm: 1–2+ inches of rain, possible heavy downpours and flooding, and thunderstorms.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the dry, warm, offshore-wind pattern and the coastal flooding threat through Friday, though exactly which areas get advisory-level winds is still being refined; the Sunday night–Monday light rain and the Tuesday–Wednesday storm are further out, with the latter called likely but its strength still uncertain.
